title: FROZEN TRAIL - 2.0 Update
body:
# FROZEN TRAIL - 2.0 Update

Raiders,

Winter has set in, bringing a substantial load of new content with it. Frozen Trail stands as the largest update since the game's launch, loaded with new features, fresh challenges, and an extensive set of fixes and improvements.

This update has been in development for a long stretch, and it is finally ready to be placed in your hands. Whether your interest lies in new content or in reviewing what has been fixed, there is material here for everyone. Settle in with something warm and read through the full breakdown below.

Thanks for playing, for reporting bugs, and for staying with the game.

# Highlights

* New map: Pendola Pass
* New map conditions: Frigate and Redirection
* New enemies: Bully, Skulker, Hydra
* New weapons: Bantam and Stiletto
* Amplified Weapons
* A revamped Skill Tree
* New items: Grappling Hook, Basic and Advanced Cameras, Tether Launcher, Yank Grenade, Mountaineer's Detector, Banjo and Harmonica
* The Outpost, including a new Research Bench
* Lootable "Design" items that unlock craftable Outpost furniture
* Improvements to the Quest System, with 22 new quests added
* A new Reward Pass system
* Weapon Stencils
* An updated default gamepad mapping
* A reworked Map Selection screen with visual and usability improvements
* The Collector DLC, available now
* Max Stash Size increased by two new levels (328 slots maximum without Expedition bonuses)

More information about Frozen Trail can be found on the official site's news section.

# Skill Tree Revamp

The Raider Skill Tree has received new skills along with improvements to existing ones, giving players more impactful options to shape their playstyle.

Feedback and player data both pointed to the Skill Tree falling short of offering genuinely interesting character-building choices. The revamp has two goals: addressing underperforming skills by modifying or replacing them, and making choice and self-expression a more central part of the Skill Tree experience.

Beyond the addition of new skills and a reorganized layout, new functionality replaces the old "large" nodes found at the middle and end of each branch. The middle of each branch now presents a single path where the node forces a binary choice between two skills. Only one can be selected, though you can revisit that choice by resetting your skill tree. At the end of each branch, two nodes require a choice among three skills; once you've invested the necessary skill points, you may pick up to two of the three.

Since this represents a major overhaul of the Skill Tree, further adjustments to both new and existing skills are likely as player engagement with the system is monitored.

# Weapon Stencils

Frozen Trail introduces Weapon Stencils, a cosmetic feature allowing players to customize their weapons' appearance with various stencil patterns. Stenciled weapons remain vulnerable like any other weapon — if you go down, another Raider can loot your weapon along with whatever stencil is applied to it.

* 14 Weapon Stencils total
* 5 Stencils are exclusive to the Frozen Trail Premium Pass
* 1 Stencil is exclusive to the DLC
* 8 Stencils can be found Topside

Stencils function much like blueprints: once learned, they can be applied to compatible weapons. Applying a Stencil requires Stencil Parts, which are found Topside.

# Outpost

The new Outpost unlocks upon completing a specific project.

* Make sure to accept the quest and bring a camera along.
* The Outpost can be expanded through different modules.
* Unlocking the Outpost also grants access to the research station.

**Furniture Designs:**

Like blueprints, Furniture Designs can be learned and then used to craft various pieces of furniture for the Outpost.

* 100 Furniture Designs have been added to the game.
* 4 Furniture Designs are exclusive to the Frozen Trail Pass.
* 1 Furniture Design is exclusive to the DLC.
* 73 Furniture Designs can be found Topside.

# Reward Pass

The Reward Pass is the new progression system, replacing and evolving the Raider Decks. Alongside this change, Cred has been removed entirely and replaced by Reward Points, a new currency applied automatically toward progress on whichever pass is currently active.

The first pass under this system is the Frozen Trail Pass, spanning 60 levels across both a Free track and a Premium track.

Existing Raider Decks have not disappeared. They have been relocated to the new Legacy Pass, with all previously unlocked rewards preserved and marked as granted. The Legacy Pass can be progressed at any time by setting it as your active pass. Note that only one Reward Pass can be active at once, so Reward Points will only count toward whichever pass is currently selected.

# Feats Rework

Feats are now divided into three categories: Easy, Medium, and Hard.

* Easy: 15 Reward Points, +1 weekly milestone progression
* Medium: 25 Reward Points, +2 weekly milestone progression
* Hard: 50 Reward Points, +3 weekly milestone progression

Weekly milestones grant 250 Reward Points each, with three available per week:

* Milestone 1: reach 4 weekly milestone progress
* Milestone 2: reach 8 weekly milestone progress
* Milestone 3: reach 12 weekly milestone progress

Once all weekly milestones are completed, Feats can still be finished, but no further major milestone rewards are granted until the weekly timer resets.

# Twitch Drops

New backpack attachments can be earned by watching your favorite streamer play ARC Raiders. Watching for at least 60 minutes grants the Oxygen Respirator, while 120 minutes grants the Mailbox. These drops run from October 8 to November 4, 2026.

# Content and Bug Fixes

## Animation

* Knockback animations now match the actual direction of the push.
* Fixed an issue where reconnecting and being revived could cause jittering and broken animations while moving.
* Fixed an issue where players could get stuck on small obstacles while sliding.
* Added animations showing the player interacting with their map and inventory.
* Added mouth animation for proximity chat speech.
* Added new contextual animations, including exhaustion after running out of breath for a while and brushing off dust after sliding.
* Fixed an issue where players kept holding items during the knockout animation or certain interactions.
* Made additional animation polish and tweaks.

## ARC

* Adjusted the Vaporizer's multi-target laser to give players a clearer window for dodging using fast traversal and dodge mechanics.
* Added fire status effect visuals for ARC drones.
* Moved higher tier loot from the leg armor pieces to the legs themselves for Queen and Matriarch.
* Since armor plates are meant to protect the legs, relocating loot to the protected area made more sense. Keeping loot inside the armor undercut the intended experience and was inconsistent with how other ARC enemies function. Armor pieces can still contain some loot.
* Improved AI sight handling to reduce rare detection errors in enemy awareness.
* The Matriarch can once again use all of its ranged attacks.
* Rebalanced physical force effects against certain ARC enemies.

## Audio

* Adjusted how character sounds are occluded by walls and obstacles for more natural audio positioning.
* Added more variation to metal groan sound effects to enhance environmental ambience.
* Added missing sound effects for the Snap Hook's attaching, detaching, and rope movement to improve audio feedback.
* Updated the Skill Tree unlock sound and added a hold-interaction audio cue in the UI.
* Fixed an issue where some weapon sounds could fail to play.
* Improved the quality of the Raider Voice model for higher fidelity voice conversion.

## Cosmetic

* Updated Celeste's appearance.
* Added an Emissive Toggle for backpacks with light sources, allowing lights to be turned off for full stealth.
* The Zenith Outfit now includes all of its intended toggles. Owners of the outfit will receive the missing toggles shortly.

## Gameplay

* "Solo vs. Squads" has been removed from the matchmaking options.
* The team wants players to have a clear incentive to use all available matchmaking settings, something Solo vs. Squads currently lacks, so its role in the game is being re-evaluated.
* Reworked the explosive damage formula against ARC. In practice, explosive weapons such as the Hullcracker now deal over 50% more damage against armor plates but around 30% less damage against more fragile parts.
* The goal is to make explosive damage feel more consistent overall while boosting its effectiveness against heavy armor. Since most ARC enemies are heavily armored, this also means slightly reduced effectiveness against weak points, in service of a more consistent numeric output.
* Adjusted some skills carried over from the previous Skill Tree to better fit the new structure:
 * Stamina gained from Fight or Flight increased by roughly 25% per level.
 * Stubborn Mule's stamina regeneration values increased by roughly 33%.
 * Back on Your Feet healing increased from 30 to 40.
* Added more contextual Ping information for ARC enemies and various objects.
* The Stash can now be upgraded by two additional tiers, bringing the new maximum (excluding Expedition rewards or acquired Nomadic Envoy space) to 328 slots.
* Loot can now be dropped to the ground directly from containers.
* Sprint-climbing ladders while exhausted is no longer possible.
* Addressed instances where vaulting onto destroyed ARC parts or other movable surfaces could unexpectedly launch or shove the player.
* Weapon slot weight reduction now applies only to the loadout; other containers and sub-containers are unaffected.
* The map can now be opened while downed.
* Improved hit registration when shooting while standing on top of ARC enemies.
* Heavy Shield: durability decay reduced from 0.20 to 0.15, and the movement penalty while equipped reduced from 15% to 10%.
* Added Scrambling: sprinting at steep slopes now allows a brief scramble up them.
* Players now automatically enter a sliding state after tumbling for too long.

## Items

* Increased Flame Spray range to better match its visual effect and improve usability.
* Ziplines now break when they intersect something after being placed.
* Reduced Snap Hook range from 20m to 18m, increased durability consumption per use from 2% to 4%, and raised power cost from 50 to 60.
* As more personal mobility items have been added, differentiating them further became necessary. The Snap Hook had previously served as a general-use mobility gadget, but with the Grappling Hook's introduction, each needed its own identity rather than existing on a simple linear upgrade path. These changes position the Snap Hook as a burst mobility gadget meant for quickly closing distance or traversing a location, with more commitment required to use it. The increased power cost still permits multiple uses in a short span at full power, but no longer allows immediate back-to-back use.
* Fixed an issue causing items to appear outside their intended areas or containers; these items are now restricted to their designated locations.

## Weapons

* Updated the Anvil's rarity from Green to Blue.
* The Anvil has proven difficult to balance. Its versatility lets it handle both Raiders and ARC effectively, outperforming weapons of its own rarity tier and above. At the same time, it remains a fan favorite and a staple of the game. Raising its rarity level places it in a better spot within the economy while preserving the gameplay and power players value. The Bantam now fills the role of the uncommon hand cannon, balanced more appropriately for that position.
* The Anvil Splitter can no longer be used as a mod; it now serves as an improved upgrade option for the Amplified Anvil, and the Tech Mod slot has been removed from the Anvil accordingly. The item itself will no longer drop but will remain available for a while so players can sell or recycle it into Amplified Fragments used to repair Amplified Weapons.
* Fixed an unintended behavior where the Jupiter's damage propagated twice to ARC parts positioned behind its intended target. As a result, the Jupiter now hits harder against armor but slightly weaker against weak spots.
* The Hullcracker no longer appears incomplete when inspected in the menu.
* Fixed an issue where the Dolabra failed to destroy the yellow weak points inside the Harvester.
* Fixed an issue where weapons picked up from the ground appeared without their attached parts.

## Maps

* Improved alignment of Doorblockers (now vertical) for small side-sliding doors.
* Improved texture quality on several maps, resolving blocky and inconsistent visuals.
* Fixed areas on several maps where players could get stuck on terrain while downed.
* Addressed areas near map edges that were darker than intended.
* Adjusted lighting on Blue Gate, refining exposure, color grading, and atmosphere.
* Fixed several spots on Blue Gate where players could get stuck.
* Fixed the Hospital Roof not being climbable.
* Restored ray-traced lighting on boarded window shutters in Buried City.
* Fixed a lighting issue in Buried City where illumination bled into an interior space.
* As mentioned in the latest Q&A, a Dynamic Loot Zone system is being tested, currently exclusive to Pendola Pass. The intent is to vary loot values in certain areas from raid to raid, making routes less predictable and scavenging more dynamic. This does not change a zone's inherent loot type — Residential loot areas remain Residential loot areas regardless — but the value a given area yields can shift between raids.
* Increased overall loot value on Riven Tides by approximately 15%.
* Fixed several spots where environmental objects could float unintentionally.

## Performance

* Implemented various optimizations affecting memory usage, general performance, and stability.
* Optimized character customization replication, fixing a bug that could cause different players to see different outfits.
* Reduced memory usage for enemies to improve stability and performance during busy encounters.
* Fixed a crash that could occur when changing graphics settings.
* Upgraded to AMD FSR version 4.1.1.

## Traders

Trader offers have been updated:

* Celeste now trades new materials used for crafting furniture and newly introduced gameplay items.
* Tian Wen no longer sells Anvil and Hullcracker offers; these will instead rotate through the weekly Nomadic Envoys.
* Launcher Ammo and Energy Clips now have a daily purchase limit.
* Shani's offers are now Coin-based and include Cameras, Light Sticks, and other social items.
* Apollo's offers now include a set of Epic Augments.
* True to their reputation, the Nomadic Envoys have let Ermal return to the trail and have instead brought in Cassio, who continues trading for valuables but will also ask friendly Raiders for help with certain quests.

## Quests

* Completing quests and quest objectives now grants XP. XP is now displayed as a visible reward in quest descriptions and shown alongside other rewards upon claiming a completed quest.
* Several older quests have been updated to require photos taken with the new camera for objectives that previously involved photographing something in the world (The League, Reduced to Rubble, Life of a Pharmacist, Battening Down, Groundbreaking).

## Social

* Fixed party join sometimes failing when accepting game invites on Xbox.
* Fixed an issue with in-game Voice Chat not working in certain instances, particularly for PS5 and Xbox players.

## UI

* Updated quest list sorting to make progression easier to follow.
* Fixed an issue where long lists could disappear while scrolling in the Settings menu.
* Fixed Nomadic Trader offers incorrectly appearing in the Acquire Resources menu.
* Emote and Quick Wheels now respond more smoothly to mouse input.
* The end-of-round screen now previews milestone progress and rewards earned that round, with milestone updates also shown in the in-round log.
* Fixed an issue where learning certain recipes displayed an incorrect "unknown not installed" message instead of a proper unlock notification, including for the Snap Hook, Blaze Grenade, and Crash Mat.
* Fixed formatting and text display issues for in-round daily quest notifications.
* Store panels now scroll when content exceeds the screen, and fixed an issue where the last toggle could be blocked and unselectable.
* Fixed an issue where not all round data reliably appeared in the End of Round Map screen.
* Fixed a bug where closing the Inventory during matchmaking could disable gamepad navigation until switching screens.

## VFX

* Fixed an issue where burning visual effects could remain stuck on other players after the effect had ended.
* Fixed an issue causing terrain textures to appear as blocky or mismatched squares on some maps at higher graphics presets.

# Dealing with Duplicated Items

Action has recently been taken to restrict accounts holding high amounts of duplicated items and to remove items obtained through duplication from player inventories. This is intended to help correct the in-game economy and clean up items that appeared through past exploits.

# Known Issues

## Gameplay

* Weapon meshes can sometimes appear partially invisible when fitted with weapon attachments.
* In rare cases, vaulting onto destroyed ARC parts and similar movable surfaces can unexpectedly launch or shove the player.
* Footsteps can become inaudible when swapping shoulders while sprinting.
* Field Repair may occasionally be unavailable after unlocking; restarting the game resolves it, and a permanent fix is in progress.
* Repairing the Tether Launcher is currently unavailable and will be fixed in an upcoming update.
* Very rarely, players may spawn into a lobby "invisibly," unable to loot, use quick wheel items, or interact with containers, though they can still fire their weapon and take damage. Returning to Speranza should restore the loadout to its state before the affected match.
* The Hydra can detect and shoot players through walls in the Cargo area.
* Standing on the side of the Cargo drop can result in instant elimination; a fix is in progress.

## Outpost

(Most fixes are already in progress and will arrive in an upcoming Live Update.)

* Unlocking the Outpost requires completing the first step, "Research Topside Living Conditions," which involves photographing a farmland house. The Camera can be purchased from Shani, crafted at the Workbench, or found Topside.
* Some furniture may clip through the Outpost structure.
* Some slots in the Outpost will be unselectable when they shouldn't be, if a piece of furniture is blocking them.
* The camera sometimes gets blocked by furniture or the character model at certain angles.
* Lighting in the main Outpost building is corrupted when Shadow quality is set to Low.
* The camera defaults back to the base room when leaving the decorating view, even if a different module was active.
* Raiders sitting at a table with chairs will clip through the table.
* The Raider steps back from the Customization view with a 10 second delay.
* The Outpost tab lacks the orange dot indicator after completing the first stage objectives needed to unlock it.

## Quests

* The cinematic fails to trigger upon completing the "Sizing Things Up" quest.
* The quest "Picking up the Pieces" cannot be completed on Pendola Pass, though it works normally on other maps; this will be fixed in an upcoming update.
* The "Damage dealt using Light Impact Grenades" feat can currently be completed using the Hullcracker.

## Audio

* Rarely, some weapons may fail to play their firing sounds on low-spec PCs, particularly the Anvil.
* Rubber Ducks can be squeezed while equipped, producing noise without needing to be thrown.

## UI

* Weapon meshes sometimes appear partially disappeared.
* Players who recently departed on the Expedition may see a notification dot on the Projects & Raider tab that does not disappear.
* Keybinds reset to default after each raid when using a non-English keyboard layout.
* The Expedition screen remains accessible through the Nomadic Envoys despite not being functional.
* The loadout weight shown in Speranza can differ slightly from what is shown in-game.
* After purchasing the Premium Reward Pass, the lock icon may still appear on premium rewards despite them being unlocked.
* The loadout weight amount differs between the Main Menu and in-round display.

## Pendola Pass

* Various clipping and collision issues.
* Vaulting onto some steep surfaces can occasionally cause players to slide back down.
* Vaulting onto destroyed ARC parts or other movable surfaces could sometimes unexpectedly launch or shove the player.

See you on Pendola Pass.
